title: Growing arrays with realloc

notes: IntList keeps the heap pointer, the length and the capacity together.
The list starts empty: data NULL, len 0, cap 0. realloc(NULL, ...) acts like malloc.
When len reaches cap, the capacity doubles: it prints 'grew to 4', 8, then 16 for ten pushes.
realloc's result goes into tmp first, so a failure can't lose the old data.
One free releases the whole array; then the fields are reset to empty.

exercises.title: Push with doubling
exercises.prompt: With IntList and list_init given, write int list_push(IntList *l, int value). If the list is full (len == cap), grow it with my_realloc: the new capacity is 4 when it was 0, otherwise double. Use the safe pattern (a temporary pointer). Then store value at the end and return 1. If growing fails, leave the list unchanged and return 0.

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++) list_push(&l, i * i); int r = l.len * 1000 + l.data[9]; my_free(l.data); r; })
tests.name: ten pushes

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); list_push(&l, 1); int a = l.cap; for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) list_push(&l, i); int r = a * 10 + l.cap; my_free(l.data); r; })
tests.name: capacity 4, then 8

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); int ok = list_push(&l, 5) + list_push(&l, 6) + list_push(&l, 7); my_free(l.data); ok; })
tests.name: returns 1 on success

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; IntList l; list_init(&l); for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) list_push(&l, i); int r = l.cap * 10 + (live_allocs - before) + (l.data[999] == 999) * 100000; my_free(l.data); r; })
tests.name: 1000 pushes: capacity 1024, one block
tests.hint_if_fail: Use my_realloc on the same block; don't allocate a new one each time.

hints: int new_cap = l->cap ? l->cap * 2 : 4; int *tmp = my_realloc(l->data, new_cap * sizeof *tmp);
if (tmp == NULL) return 0; l->data = tmp; l->cap = new_cap; then l->data[l->len++] = value;

exercises.title: Get safely, free completely
exercises.prompt: list_push is done for you. Write int list_get(const IntList *l, int i, int *out): if i is a valid index (0 to len - 1) store the item in *out and return 1; otherwise leave *out alone and return 0. Then write void list_free(IntList *l): free the data with my_free and reset data to NULL, len and cap to 0, so calling it twice is safe.

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); list_push(&l, 7); list_push(&l, 9); int v = -1; int ok = list_get(&l, 1, &v); my_free(l.data); ok * 100 + v; })
tests.name: gets an item

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); list_push(&l, 7); list_push(&l, 9); int v = -1; int ok = list_get(&l, 2, &v); my_free(l.data); ok * 100 + v; })
tests.name: past the end
tests.hint_if_fail: Valid indexes are 0 to len - 1, not cap - 1.

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; IntList l; list_init(&l); for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) list_push(&l, i); list_free(&l); (live_allocs - before) + l.len + l.cap + (l.data != NULL); })
tests.name: frees and resets

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); list_push(&l, 3); int v = -1; int ok = list_get(&l, -1, &v); my_free(l.data); ok * 100 + v; })
tests.name: negative index

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; IntList l; list_init(&l); list_push(&l, 1); list_free(&l); list_free(&l); list_push(&l, 2); int r = l.len * 10 + l.data[0]; list_free(&l); r * 10 + (live_allocs - before); })
tests.name: free twice, then reuse

hints: list_free: my_free(l->data); l->data = NULL; l->len = 0; l->cap = 0;

exercises.title: Drop the glitches
exercises.prompt: A soil sensor sometimes sends nonsense. list_push is done for you. Write int list_filter(IntList *l, int lo, int hi): keep only the values from lo to hi (inclusive), in their original order, moving them down inside the same array (no new allocation). Update len and return how many were removed. An empty list (data NULL) removes 0.

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); int v[] = {12, 99, 15, -40, 14}; for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) list_push(&l, v[i]); int removed = list_filter(&l, 0, 50); int r = removed * 1000 + l.len * 100 + l.data[2]; my_free(l.data); r; })
tests.name: removes two glitches

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); int v[] = {12, 99, 15, -40, 14}; for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) list_push(&l, v[i]); list_filter(&l, 0, 50); int r = l.data[0] * 100 + l.data[1]; my_free(l.data); r; })
tests.name: keeps the order
tests.hint_if_fail: Keep a write index: copy each good value to data[w++].

tests.call: ({ IntList l; list_init(&l); for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) list_push(&l, 500); int removed = list_filter(&l, 0, 50); my_free(l.data); removed * 10 + l.len; })
tests.name: everything removed

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; IntList l; list_init(&l); list_push(&l, 0); list_push(&l, 50); list_push(&l, 51); int removed = list_filter(&l, 0, 50); int r = removed * 100 + l.len * 10 + (live_allocs - before); my_free(l.data); r; })
tests.name: limits inclusive, no new block

hints: Use two indexes: r reads every item, w is where the next kept item goes.
if (l->data[r] >= lo && l->data[r] <= hi) l->data[w++] = l->data[r];

quiz.q: What's the difference between len and cap?
choices: len is how many items are in use; cap is how many fit before growing
cap is in bytes, len in items
len can be bigger than cap

quiz.q: Why double the capacity instead of adding 1?
choices: Far fewer reallocs (and copies) as the array grows
quiz.why: Doubling makes pushes cheap on average.

quiz.q: What's wrong with l->data = realloc(l->data, n);?
choices: If realloc fails, data becomes NULL and the old block leaks
quiz.why: Use a temporary and only assign on success.

quiz.q: You keep int *first = &l.data[0]; then push 100 more items. What about first?
choices: It may point at freed memory, because realloc can move the block
It moves along with the data
quiz.why: Keep indexes into a growing array, not pointers.
That lets an empty list start with data = NULL.

cards.q: Three fields of a dynamic array?

cards.a: tmp = realloc(p, n); if (tmp == NULL) handle it; else p = tmp;
When len == cap, double cap (start at something like 4).
free(data); then data = NULL, len = cap = 0.

explain: Explain in your own words why the safe realloc pattern needs a temporary pointer, with a made-up example of what goes wrong without it.
